facts.fact: CPJ describes Decree-Law 54 as Tunisia's cybercrime law, under which prosecutions of journalists proceeded in 2026.
CPJ says Ghassen Ben Khelifa was sentenced to two years on 30 March 2026 under Decree-Law 54 for false news and harming public security.
CPJ reports a run of Decree-Law 54 convictions from July 2025 to 2026, including Ramla Dahmani, Khaoula Boukrim (four years, 26 February 2026), Ben Khelifa and Sonia Dahmani.
CPJ says the Sfax Court of Appeal sentenced commentator Haythem el-Mekki on 8 July 2026 to one year over a social media post denouncing failings at a hospital.
CPJ says Sonia Dahmani received an 18-month sentence on appeal in April 2026 over remarks on migrants and another two-year sentence in May 2026 over remarks on prison conditions.
CPJ says journalists Zied el-Heni, Mourad Zghidi and Borhen Bsaies are currently behind bars in Tunisia.
